newsitem.title: USA: IBM has e-mail problems on Internet service.
newsitem.headline: IBM has e-mail problems on Internet service.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. confirmed Thursday it is having problems with electronic mail on its Internet access service -- one day after PC World magazine gave the little-known service a top rating.
Late Wednesday, CNET, an Internet-based technology news service, reported that an unspecified number of users of the IBM Internet Connection were experiencing delays in receiving e-mail.

An IBM spokeswoman confirmed that the Armonk, N.Y.-based company has had some problems delivering e-mail to Internet Connection subscribers, but said IBM has had "no reports of significant mail loss."
She said she did not know how many customers were affected by the problems.

"We have been aware that there have been slowdowns," the spokeswoman said, adding that the problems were "sporadic" and were likely triggered after IBM switched to a flat-rate pricing plan of $19.95 a month last July. IBM does not disclose how many subscribers its service has.
The spokeswoman said IBM is upgrading its network to speed the delivery of e-mail and increase the service's capacity for storing it.
PC World gave IBM glowing reviews in its February issue, which hits newsstands on Tuesday.

The magazine said IBM's Internet access service was the winner among 12 leading services in a survey of 3,800 online users, who gave the IBM Internet Connection an A-plus rating. PC World also rated the service a "Best Buy," along with Mindspring's service.
"This kind of stuff can happen to any ISP," Brad Grimes, senior associate editor at PC World, said Thursday, referring to the e-mail problems.

"We haven't gotten any complaints ... and in IBM's case, we did not have any e-mail lost," Grimes said, adding that PC World staff members ran their own tests of e-mail over all the Internet services surveyed over a two-week period.

Analysts said IBM was not alone with e-mail problems over the increasingly congested Internet. Last November, half of the 425,000 users of AT&T Corp.'s WorldNet service were hit by a problem in AT&T's computers that temporarily halted e-mail delivery.
"It's another day in life on the 'Net," said Ted Julian, an analyst with International Data Corp.
